A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 19-page paper, including references and Appendices A–B. All substantive text, equations, and Table 1 match; the differences are confined to the marginal arXiv stamp and its version link.

before.justification: Section 4.5 reports original GoEmotions gratitude experiments. Section 5, Table 1, and Appendix B also report the authors' original coding and analysis of 17 papers.

after.justification: Retains the original GoEmotions experiments in Section 4.5 and the 17-paper coding results in Section 5, Table 1, and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The three-phase Construct Validity Protocol, intervention strategies in Section 3.3, and Counterfactual Neutralization formula in Equation 4 are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate gratitude on GoEmotions and analyze the same 17-paper literature corpus. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 4.5 retains the same nuisance-only and nuisance-plus-proxy comparisons. No evaluated comparison method is added, removed, or revised.

E3.justification: Both retain the 43,410/5,426/5,427 GoEmotions split and the eight-variant stability evaluation on 2,000 test examples. Encoder, pooling, normalization, nuisance-control, and metric settings match, as does Appendix A's coding rubric.

E4.justification: The encoder/pooling/normalization sensitivity analysis, separate nuisance-block analyses, and high/low/borderline examples with false positives and false negatives in Section 4.5 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same ICC estimation forms for eight instrument variants and retain identical confidence-interval recommendations. No seed, repeated-run, significance-testing, or uncertainty-reporting information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. Both report nuisance-only and nuisance-plus-proxy AUCs of 0.9658 and 0.9831, respectively, and ICC values of 0.8467 and 0.9779. Table 1's counts and every Appendix B rating are unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 1's isotropic-Gaussian assumptions and rotational-ambiguity proof are identical. The cosine/Euclidean decompositions and validity equations also remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about non-identification, Counterfactual Neutralization, the CVP/Validity Suite, and the forensic literature review.

C2.justification: Interpretations of nuisance surrogacy and metric indeterminacy are unchanged. Both retain the same coding limitations and acknowledge that the full CVP has not been instantiated end to end on a new dataset.

D1.justification: Section 4.5 discloses the same encoder names, pooling and normalization choices, nuisance-feature construction, and sample counts. Appendix A's coding instructions are identical, with no changes to implementation or code/data access information.

R1.justification: The bibliography, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to measurement theory, causal representation learning, and NLP validity research are identical. The paper-level assessments in Appendix B also match.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv identifier/date changes from v1, 8 May 2026, to v2, 9 July 2026. The title, authors, article prose, section order, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes position on page 1. The article layout, equations, and Table 1 remain identical; rendered pages 2–19, including both appendices, are pixel-identical.

improvement.justification: The only differences are the arXiv version/date stamp, its placement, and its associated version link. Scientific content, empirical evidence, mathematical arguments, limitations, and appendices are identical, leaving overall paper quality unchanged.
